examples.solution_text:
The equally spaced ticks increase by $10$, then $20$, then $10$. Equal distances represent unequal changes, so the scale is uneven.
Use equally spaced labels $0,10,20,30,40$. Keep tea at $10$ orders and juice at $30$ orders, and redraw the bars using that scale.

Stall A sold $8$ boxes and Stall B sold $12$. Stall B's bar is also wider, making its area exaggerate the difference.
Redraw the bars with equal widths and even gaps. Keep their heights at $8$ and $12$ so height alone shows the number sold.

examples.question_text:
A school poster shows $4$ large ball symbols for football viewers and $7$ small ball symbols for tennis viewers. It gives no key.
Explain two features that prevent a fair, reliable comparison.
examples.solution_text:
The symbols have different sizes, so football can look more popular even though it has fewer symbols.
There is no key saying how many viewers each symbol represents, so viewer totals cannot be calculated. Use equal-sized symbols and a clear key with the same number of viewers per symbol.

examples.question_text:
A library recorded visitor numbers on six days: Monday $18$, Tuesday $21$, Wednesday $19$, Thursday $20$, Friday $46$ and Saturday $49$.
Its website shows only Friday and Saturday and claims, “We have more than $40$ visitors every day.” Explain why the display and claim are misleading.
examples.solution_text:
The display selects only the two busiest days and leaves out four days with fewer than $40$ visitors. This is cherry picking.
The claim is false: Monday to Thursday had only $18$ to $21$ visitors per day. Show all six days to give a fair account of the recorded week.

coverage.summary: Authored five worked examples covering all seven distinct assessed methods using Stage 3 arithmetic and language. Questions and solutions are separate editable fields; solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue. Native diagrams use black outlines, 10 pt ordinary labels and 8.5 pt ticks. The corrected graph and value annotations appear only in the solution. Independent equations need no phantom continuation gutters. Relevant supplied source images were inspected; source answers were not copied uncritically. Practice and quiz content were classified only and remain unchanged. Independent review and final rendered verification remain for the coordinator.

examples.derivation: The question scale gives Monday 84 and Tuesday 92. Their drawn heights above 80 are 1 and 3, but 92−84=8 and 3×84=252, so the tripling claim is false. On the corrected scale, 25 items occupy 0.8 cm: 84×0.032=2.688 cm and 92×0.032=2.944 cm, matching the bars and solution annotations. This follows source Q1's numerical comparison and Q12's fair-display selection.

Equal drawing intervals carry labels 0, 10, 30 and 40, giving successive increases of 10, 20 and 10. The bars end at 10 and 30. Equally spaced labels 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40 repair the scale while preserving those values. This adapts source Q4b.

The scale represents 4 boxes per centimetre, so bar heights 2 and 3 represent 8 and 12 boxes. Their widths are 0.7 and 2.1 cm. The wider second bar exaggerates the comparison through area; equal widths preserve a comparison based on height. This adapts source Q4d.

Four large symbols can visually outweigh seven small symbols, so symbol size can distort the comparison. Without a key, neither symbol count determines a viewer total. Equal-sized symbols and a common stated value per symbol address both defects. Source Q7 supports the size comparison; the missing-key adaptation covers the retained accepted assessment method.

Only Friday's 46 and Saturday's 49 exceed 40. The four omitted observations are 18, 21, 19 and 20, all below 40, directly refuting the claim about every day. Showing all six observations repairs the selective account. This applies the cherry-picking feature explicitly taught at source line 63.

review.summary: All 21 exact assessment locators are mapped, and the five examples cover all seven distinct assessed methods. No existing examples require dispositions. The new examples use Stage 3 reasoning, separate editable questions and solutions, supported inline mathematics, and appropriate diagram specifications. Example 0 contains independent equations, so no phantom continuation gutter is needed. Solution prose and mathematics inherit the implemented blue styling; diagram ink remains black. Accepted practice and quiz mathematics were not re-audited. Final rendered typography and layout verification remain with the coordinator.
